input.rationale: Corrective update: the previous submission's gap answer for this question contained a malformed receipt reference (a duplicated identifier fragment), which is a transcription blemish in the research record rather than a change of evidence. This version restates the same answer with the three acknowledgement receipts and the two divergence receipts named once each, and leaves every comparison, execution index, counterevidence item and limitation unchanged.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: In this scenario and window no acknowledged entry was lost after healing: two seconds after the partition healed, the isolated node and the majority-side leader each still held their own acknowledged entry in their own log store, neither had applied an entry absent from its own log, and the flag-off control's isolated side never acknowledged an entry.
knowledge.conditions: Five-voter committed configuration with a three-voter snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the restarted node isolated with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns and both sides acknowledging a distinct client write; two second apply timeout and two second heal settle; in-memory log stores.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: Four completed comparisons with controls establish the defect, and three further completed comparisons bound its consequences. Configuration: receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 15 - the node restarted from a log whose latest configuration is index 14 with five servers came back at configuration index 1 with three servers - control holding at evaluated event index 18. Election: receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 22 - the node isolated with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returned became leader with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3, with majority_side_leader also true - control holding at index 25. Single-side acknowledgement: receipt 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 27 - the isolated leader's Apply completed - control holding at index 29. Two-sided acknowledgement: receipt f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 27 - both sides acknowledged a client write concurrently - control holding at index 29. Bounds on durability: receipt 4e9eaa72cf594018b8414a8d8efb7cb3 has all three comparisons holding - neither node applied an entry absent from its own log and each still held its acknowledged entry two seconds after healing (evaluated event index 27), while the control's isolated side never acknowledged (index 29) - so no lost entry or applied-without-log divergence was produced in this schedule, and none is claimed. Source: restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the startup scan at api.go:604-620, so AddVoter's later entry (api.go:994-1005) is never re-read and the node keeps the snapshot's three-server list; quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) then returns two, electSelf (raft.go:1999-2060) asks only that list, and the commitment calculation (commitment.go:78-104) accepts two matching indexes, so leadership and acknowledgements rest on a majority of an obsolete configuration. The manoeuvre the runs needed - also cutting the single committed voter off from the majority side so requestVote's existing-leader guard (raft.go:1690-1700) does not refuse the vote - is an ordinary partition shape, and the minority leadership appeared in every immediate-isolation execution and in none of the settled-schedule executions.

7da03e78394f41fdad540ae0824ec2a6-gap-1.explanation: Both parts are answered by receipts. Election and acknowledgement: receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 (violated at witness event index 22, control holding at 25), receipt 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db (violated at witness index 27, control holding at 29) and receipt f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c (violated at witness index 27, control holding at 29, both sides acknowledging). Reproduction depends on whether the single committed voter on the isolated side still hears the majority-side leader, because requestVote refuses candidates while a leader is known (raft.go:1690-1700): with isolation applied immediately after the restart it reproduced in every execution, with the settled schedule it did not. Divergence: receipt a608e5f60ae4415981c1024522a24a0d shows the two nodes holding different entries at the same log index eight seconds after healing while both sides had acknowledged, with the flag-off control agreeing at its index; receipt 4e9eaa72cf594018b8414a8d8efb7cb3 shows the two-second window is a negative for both loss and applied-without-log divergence. The witnessed divergence is therefore two logs retaining different entries rather than a lost acknowledged entry, and the compared payloads are emitted only as a derived boolean.

counterevidence: The flag-off controls in all five receipts keep the committed configuration, cannot win on the isolated side and do not acknowledge there.

The durability bound is negative in the observed window: both acknowledged entries survived in their own logs and no applied-without-log divergence appeared, so the lost-entry consequence is not established.

Two settled-schedule executions did not produce the minority leadership, and the difference is explained by whether the isolated partner still heard the majority-side leader; no frequency or absence claim is made.
limitations: Every observation is bounded (three second majority-leader wait, five second election window, two second apply timeout, two or eight second heal settle), so no occurrence-rate or absence bound is established.
Log agreement after healing is asserted from a native probe of the eight-second window and awaits a receipt; the earlier two-second window produced a negative, so the observation is window dependent.
The scenario restarts the former leader of a cluster grown by adding voters; other roles, change types, chain orders and durable stores are not explored.
interpretations.joint_history: Five complete executions of the same five-voter scenario over identical stores, sizes and snapshot timing supply the seven comparisons: b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 (configuration loss and control), abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 (election and control), 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db (single-side acknowledgement and control), f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c (two-sided acknowledgement and control) and 4e9eaa72cf594018b8414a8d8efb7cb3 (durability bounds and control). Each receipt built its own cluster and stores and is a complete history in itself; only the comparison declarations, the bounded windows and the result event names differ, and the configuration values agree across all five (flagged side at index 1 with three servers against expected 14 with five; controls at 14 with five), so none is a fragment of another.

scope.description: Five-voter cluster whose leading node is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a snapshot predating the membership change, isolated with one committed voter immediately after the restart; both sides acknowledge a distinct client write, the partition heals, and after eight seconds the event reports whether the two nodes' logs hold different entries at the same index, whether either node applied an entry absent from its own log, and the leadership and acknowledgement outcomes. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: A successful Apply is an acknowledgement to the client.
Two nodes holding different entries at the same log index after healing is a violation of log agreement.
Eight seconds is enough for AppendEntries exchange between the two sides.
excluded: Entry contents at the conflict index, which the probe reports as empty strings.
Any claim about durable stores; the in-memory stores are used.

experiment.prefix: The harness reuses the multi-voter scenario construction and the two-sided apply, then scans each side's log store for its own acknowledged entry, compares the two nodes' entries at the isolated side's last index, and emits logs_differ_at_conflict_index with the per-side log and FSM survival flags, the applied-without-log operands, and the leadership and acknowledgement outcomes. No production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns log agreement: after a partition heals, two replicas of the committed configuration must not hold different entries at the same index, especially when both writes were acknowledged to clients.

comparisons.description: After healing, the two nodes must agree at the index where the isolated side wrote; the defect prediction is that they hold different entries there.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side never writes, so the two logs cannot differ at that index.

experiment.revision_reason: The heal settle is extended from two to eight seconds so a losing suffix has time to be truncated, and the event now carries logs_differ_at_conflict_index, which compares the two nodes' log entries at the index where the isolated side wrote. Scenario, isolation, waits and the two-sided apply are unchanged.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. The probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the formal comparison is left to the submitted experiment. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node's own membership view is the pre-restart snapshot value or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) prevent it from campaigning, and quorumSize() is computed over a configuration that contradicts the committed log (raft.go:1087-1094). Counterevidence examined: a snapshot can legitimately supply the configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot; appendEntries processes only entries it newly appends (raft.go:1594-1621); leaderLoop only promotes latest to committed (raft.go:797-799). Limitations: the finding is scoped to the stated configuration and store conditions; the snapshot-present variant remains a registered gap; only a controller receipt can make this a completed comparison.

The retained receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f (exit 0) contains the four emitted events, and the two result events witness the predicted difference under identical inputs: event 1 (mode on, restore_committed_logs true, snapshots 0) reports after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0, after_has_vote false with after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11, while event 3 (mode off) reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1, after_has_vote true. The admission events (0 and 2) confirm both cases started from before_latest_index 1 with one server, so the only difference is whether restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied. Source reading explains the mechanism: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped, and processLogs never updates r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The receipt s declared comparisons returned unknown rather than violated: the controller reported "No corresponding prerequisite events reached: mode_on/startup_before_restart" for both on-case comparisons and the analogous message for the off-case control, because the compared identity included phase and the admission events carry phase before_restart while the result events carry after_restart. That is a declaration defect, not missing evidence, so the raw observations are retained and a successor experiment with identity_fields [mode] is submitted for a fresh, complete comparison; no completed comparison is claimed here. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node holds an empty (or snapshot-age) membership view, so runFollower's "no known peers, aborting election" branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) leave it unable to campaign, and quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) is computed over a configuration that contradicts its own committed log.
counterevidence: A restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the configuration (event 3), which isolates the flagged recovery path rather than the restart itself.
A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678), but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot.
limitations: The comparison outcomes in this receipt are unknown; a completed comparison waits on the successor experiment.
Only the single-node, no-snapshot case is witnessed; the snapshot-present variant remains the registered gap.
The separate suspicion that restoreFromCommittedLogs' processLogs call can block NewRaft before runFSM starts is untested and outside this claim.

Its events 0-3 repeat the no-snapshot pair with the same values as receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175: mode on yields after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0 and after_has_vote false while after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11 were restored, and the mode off control yields index 1 with one voter. Events 4 and 5 cover the snapshot-present case: before shutdown the log's latest configuration is index 1227 with two servers while the snapshot sits at index 1220 with configuration index 1 (one server), and after the restart the node reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1 and matches_committed_log false, so both declared comparisons are violated by witness event index 5 with admission event index 4. The mechanism is the one the source predicts: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 because restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) has already advanced lastApplied to the persisted commit index; processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM without ever updating r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The node therefore resumes with a membership view that its own committed log contradicts: in the witnessed case it drops a committed membership change (an added nonvoter) that postdates its snapshot, and in the no-snapshot case it resumes with no peers at all, which runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) turn into a permanent inability to campaign, with quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) computed over the stale configuration. interpretations.rationale: Source: NewRaft's FSM queue is created with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines are only started after the startup work at api.go:632-639; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A committed backlog needing more than 128 batches therefore has no consumer while NewRaft runs. A native construction probe with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 measured a sharp boundary: 8002 committed entries (126 batches) returned from NewRaft in 3 ms, while 8402 entries (132 batches) had not returned after a bounded 15 second wait. That probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the submitted experiment repeats both sizes under controller execution and only its receipt can make this a completed comparison.
counterevidence: A backlog that stays at or below the queue capacity returns promptly, so the failure is not general slowness of log replay.
limitations: No receipt yet; the account rests on source reading plus a native probe.
The interval is a bounded wait, not an infinite-run proof; a later repair or a substantially different schedule is not excluded.
The queue capacity is taken from the source constant, not measured.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 04fccedbacf54df3b7064fd16fa57b26 (exit 0, ten events, no parse loss) witnesses the prediction: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, no snapshot, 8402 committed entries and a restored commit index of 8402 (event index 8), the restart reported newraft_returned false after a bounded 15 second wait (event index 9), so comparison 0 is violated with witness event index 9. The paired below-capacity case is retained as an observation, not as a completed comparison: event index 7 reports newraft_returned true after 0 ms for 8002 entries, but comparison 1 returned unknown because both backlog cases shared one result event name, so each comparison looked for the other case's admission and the controller marked the other result incomplete; the corrected declaration gives each size its own result event and is submitted as a successor experiment. Source mechanism: NewRaft creates fsmMutateCh with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and starts the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines only after the startup work at api.go:632-639, while restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A replay needing more than 128 batches therefore blocks on an unconsumed channel inside NewRaft, with no retry, timeout or fallback in that path. Consequence under the stated conditions: the node never finishes starting, so a node that should resume service after a restart does not, and every duty depending on it (elections, replication, convergence) is stalled indefinitely rather than bounded; with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 the boundary sits near 8192 committed entries and the default TrailingLogs of 10240 allows a log that large before any snapshot.
counterevidence: The sub-capacity case returned immediately (0 ms for 8002 entries), so the outcome is not general slowness of replaying committed logs.
No snapshot existed in either case, so the blocking is independent of snapshot restore.
limitations: The failing case is a bounded 15 second wait, not an infinite-run proof; a different schedule or a later repair is not excluded by this observation alone.
The queue capacity of 128 and the batch size are taken from the source, not measured.
The configuration-loss finding under the parent question is a separate defect and is not part of this account.

That probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the submitted experiment re-runs both cases under controller execution; only its receipt can make this comparison complete.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt f5cb1459db5e418d9a9aa6987ef76dfc (exit 0, fourteen events, no parse loss) settles both comparisons. Comparison 0 is violated by witness event index 11: after restarting the single-voter node with RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, became_leader is false and the final state is Follower across the whole 1500 ms sampling window, with after_latest_index 0 (admission event is the matching startup_before_restart with before_latest_index 1). Comparison 1 holds at evaluated event index 13: the identical restart without the flag reports became_leader true, final state Leader and after_latest_index 1, so the difference tracks the recovery flag and not restart timing. Source mechanism: with an empty latest configuration, runFollower's first branch logs 'no known peers, aborting election' and never sets Candidate (raft.go:228-232); even if it reached the candidate path, quorumSize() would be 1 while electSelf asks only the servers in the same empty configuration, so no vote is ever counted (raft.go:1087-1094); and the configuration is empty precisely because restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied past the committed LogConfiguration before the startup scan (api.go:604-620 and 724-754). Consequence under the witnessed conditions: a single-voter cluster that restarts with this flag never regains a leader, so all client duties that require a leader stay pending indefinitely; the pending duty is not merely delayed but has no enabled path to completion, since the node's own committed log holds the configuration it would need. The same source branch applies to a node in a larger cluster, where it would remain unable to campaign and would also compute an empty quorum, but only the single-voter case is witnessed here.
counterevidence: The flag-off control reaches Leader inside the same 1500 ms window, so the non-campaigning is not a general restart delay.

The library deliberately grants votes when the server list is empty (bootstrap affordance), which explains why such a node still answers vote requests; the witnessed defect is the state itself, not the vote-granting rule.
limitations: Only a single-voter configuration is exercised, so an election run under a stale multi-voter membership is not witnessed.
The window is bounded at 1500 ms against a 50 ms election timeout, so a much later recovery is not excluded.
The same experiment keeps no snapshot; the snapshot-age configuration variant is witnessed only through the configuration observation, not through this authority sample.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. The probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the formal comparison is left to the submitted experiment. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node's own membership view is the pre-restart snapshot value or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) prevent it from campaigning, and quorumSize() is computed over a configuration that contradicts the committed log (raft.go:1087-1094). Counterevidence examined: a snapshot can legitimately supply the configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot; appendEntries processes only entries it newly appends (raft.go:1594-1621); leaderLoop only promotes latest to committed (raft.go:797-799). Limitations: the finding is scoped to the stated configuration and store conditions; the snapshot-present variant remains a registered gap; only a controller receipt can make this a completed comparison.
